decisions.executionNote: Holder is in right workspace, pens on left. Begin right-hand side-grasp approach with gradual inward-facing wrist rotation; left stays at origin.
Advance right hand toward the holder's right side, completing the horizontal side-grasp orientation while remaining open.
Replan from interrupted pose with smaller translation and a less extreme wrist yaw. Approach holder diagonally to preserve joint margin.
Holder appears disturbed at contact. Close right gripper in place and make a short test lift; inspect actual retention and uprightness before transfer.
Test lift shows empty jaws; holder has tipped forward. Reopen and approach its visible body farther forward and right, using small continuous steps.
Align jaws lower and farther forward around the tipped holder body, close, and test a small lift. Retention remains uncertain.
Lift and retract the closed right hand to verify holder retention and obtain room to restore its upright orientation.
Holder remains on table, now sideways. Switch to an overhead barrel grasp, opening jaws and rotating gradually while clear of it.
Previous rotation was rejected without motion. Reduce rotation increments fourfold and gain clearance before continuing overhead alignment.
Continue overhead alignment above the sideways holder, keeping the elbow configuration continuous.
Finish downward grasp orientation and approach above the holder body, leaving clearance before final descent.
Pause rotation after continuity guard. Descend at the accepted oblique overhead orientation, aligning the finger center over the holder body.
Descent met resistance above the far end. Recenter toward the nearer middle of the holder before another shallow descent, keeping jaws open.
The holder now lies between the open fingers. Descend slightly, close fully, and test retention with a short upward motion.
Holder appears retained between the fingers. Raise and bring it closer while gently rotating its far end upward; inspect opening orientation next.
Holder was not retained. Reopen and establish a more vertical overhead grasp, accounting for the link-to-finger offset before descending deeper.
Complete vertical alignment and descend over the holder's middle with open jaws, avoiding the earlier shallow contact.
Close around the holder at the deeper vertical grasp, allow closure to settle, then lift without rotating to check retention.
The deeper grasp appears to lift the holder. Keep closed while raising, retracting toward the shared boundary, and rotating the opening upward.
Holder is visibly retained. Complete the upward rotation while bringing it nearer the robot, keeping the grasp closed and the left arm clear.
Turn the retained holder toward the shared boundary and lower it to a convenient filling height. Begin the left-arm approach to the blue pens without crossing arms.
The holder opening is visible and upright. Stabilize it nearer the boundary while moving the left hand above the nearer blue pen and turning toward an overhead grasp.
Keep the right-hand holder steady and finish the left overhead approach to the cap-side body of the nearer blue pen.
Align the left fingers vertically and descend slowly around the blue pen body. Keep the holder fixed and closed in the right hand.
Center the blue pen between the left fingers, close fully, and lift to verify retention before orienting it for insertion.
Blue pen is visibly retained. Raise it clear of the table and rotate the capped end upward while approaching the holder from the left.
Bring the upright blue pen above the opening. Gently correct the holder's visible lean while keeping its rim approximately stationary and both grasps closed.
Lower the blue pen toward the upright opening with a small forward centering adjustment. Hold the holder fixed; retain the pen until its lower end is visibly inside.
Center the pen's lower end slightly left and back, then insert it slowly while keeping the upright holder stationary.
Release the first blue pen inside the holder and withdraw the left fingers up and left, checking that the pen remains in the cup.
First pen remains in the upright holder. Move the open left hand above the remaining blue pen and begin the overhead grasp rotation.
Replan after the continuity guard using half-sized rotations and reduced translation; continue toward the remaining blue pen with clearance.
Continue rotating the left fingers downward and position over the cap-side portion of the remaining blue pen; maintain clearance while the holder stays fixed.
Finish the near-vertical left grasp and descend around the blue pen's cap-side body, using small increments and keeping the right holder stationary.
Center the second blue pen between the fingers, close fully, and make a small test lift before transport.
The second blue pen is retained. Lift clear of the table, retract toward the filling area, and begin turning the cap upward.
Complete the cap-up rotation and move the second blue pen above the holder, leaving vertical clearance for visual alignment.
Center the second pen's lower end over the free side of the opening and lower toward the rim, correcting its residual tilt while retaining the grasp.
Insert the second blue pen slowly into the free space, with a small leftward centering correction. Keep the holder upright and both grasps closed until seated.
Release the second blue pen within the opening, then withdraw up and left. Keep the right-hand holder steady and check that both pens remain inside.
Both blue pens remain in the holder. Move the open left hand toward the farther black-and-yellow pen and begin its overhead grasp alignment.
Align the left fingers with the farther yellow pen's cap-side body and descend to a safe overhead pregrasp. The right holder remains fixed.
Finish the vertical overhead grasp and lower around the farther yellow pen's cap-side barrel. Keep fingers open until the next close-and-lift check.
Shift slightly toward the yellow pen's cap and center it between the fingers, close fully, then lift a short distance to verify the grasp.
The forward adjustment reached an IK boundary. Grasp at the accepted barrel position instead, then lift and retract toward a less extended configuration to check retention.
The yellow pen is retained. Lift and retract it away from the table, turning its cap upward while preserving clearance from the filled holder.
Complete the yellow pen's cap-up orientation and move above the unfilled near-left side of the opening, leaving clearance for final visual alignment.
Center the yellow pen's lower end over the free near-left part of the opening and lower toward the rim, keeping both grasps closed.
Lower the yellow pen farther into the free slot, then open the left fingers while holding position so it can settle inside the upright holder.
The yellow pen and holder shifted on release. Withdraw the left hand clear to assess settling and retention before attempting the last pen.
Yellow pen fell back to the table; the two blue pens remain retained. Correct the holder's new leftward lean with the right wrist before another insertion attempt.
Use smaller right-wrist corrections after the continuity interruption. Move the left hand clear above the remaining lengthwise yellow pen to prepare a new grasp.
Align the left hand along the lengthwise yellow pen before pitching downward. Keep the two-pen holder upright and stationary.
Pitch the open left gripper toward an overhead grasp of the lengthwise yellow pen, keeping its cap-side barrel as the target and the holder steady.
Finish the vertical grasp alignment and descend over the yellow pen's cap-side barrel, staying clear of the other pen and the holder.
Descend the final short distance around the yellow barrel, close the left gripper, and test retention with a small lift while the holder stays fixed.
Lift the retained yellow pen clear, retract away from the holder, and rotate its cap upward. Keep the right hand stationary and closed.
Finish bringing the retained yellow pen upright with its cap upward, staying above and to the left of the holder before the lateral alignment.
Turn the upright yellow pen toward the holder and align above its free side. Maintain height and closed grippers until the lower end is centered.
Lower the yellow pen into the free right side of the opening with a small lateral correction. Stop above finger-to-rim contact and inspect before releasing.
The yellow pen's lower end is inside the free slot. Seat it a little farther, release in place, and withdraw up-left while keeping the holder steady.
Three pens remain in the holder. Clear the opening and begin aligning the open left hand for the last yellow pen lying nearer the robot.
Continue matching the last pen's diagonal axis while approaching from above. Keep the three-pen holder fixed and the left fingers open.
After the continuity guard, pause yaw and gently pitch downward using smaller increments. Approach the last pen's cap-side barrel without extending either arm.
Continue the downward approach while refining alignment with the last pen's diagonal axis. Keep the fingers open and the three-pen holder stable.
Finish the vertical overhead alignment and descend around the final pen's cap-side barrel, keeping the holder still and the left fingers open.
Center the final yellow barrel between the left fingers, close fully, and lift a short distance to verify retention before transport.
Lift the retained final pen clear of the table and begin rotating its cap upward, retracting away from the holder to maintain clearance.
Complete the cap-up rotation of the final pen at safe height, keeping it clear of the holder before turning toward the opening.
Pause the pitch after the continuity guard and turn the held pen gradually toward the holder, moving away from the wrist's difficult configuration before finishing upright alignment.
Reduce wrist yaw increments to one third after the guard; keep the retained final pen at constant height while traversing the sensitive wrist configuration.
Continue the gradual turn toward the holder now that the sensitive wrist region has eased; keep the final pen retained and clear of the rim.
Turn the retained final pen above the holder's remaining free side, keeping it elevated before correcting its small residual tilt and lowering.
Straighten the last pen and center its lower end over the remaining slot, lowering only slightly for a visual check before seating.
The final pen's lower end appears within the opening. Seat only a few millimeters, release, and withdraw up-left to inspect whether all four remain in the upright holder.
The last pen fell outside the cup. Move the retained three-pen holder rightward to expose it, while aligning the left hand above the pen's left-side barrel for recovery.
The loose pen has rolled into the right workspace. Prepare a careful holder handover at the center boundary so the right hand can recover it without crossing arms.
Lower the left fingers around the holder's upper body and close while the right hand continues supporting it. Verify the overlapping support before releasing the right hand.
Transfer support to the closed left hand: open and retreat the right fingers, then move the holder leftward. Inspect retention before the right arm approaches the loose pen.
